name: Crossover Lore: Knowing the Other Kind

pages.name: Crossover Lore: Knowing the Other Kind

text.content:
The Storytellers Guide's "Those Who Hunt the Night" chapter is largely Storyteller-facing advice on running crossover stories with werewolves, changelings, wraiths, mages and psychics — why to allow them, how to keep them from degenerating into everyday occurrences, and how to balance Storyteller-character and player-character power levels. That guidance isn't reproduced here as it contains no dice mechanics. It does, however, define one reusable, table-usable framework: using specific Lore Abilities (rather than blanket "the Storyteller decides") to calibrate how much a character actually knows about another supernatural type.

Lore Abilities as a Knowledge Dial

Different Lore Abilities represent different depths and accuracy of knowledge about other supernatural creatures, and a Kindred's specific Lore (rather than general Occult) determines what she actually knows versus what's folklore or propaganda:

  • Occult (general): A Kindred with four or more levels might correctly suspect that lycanthropes are real and that legends like a vulnerability to silver hold some truth — vague, mostly-right suspicion rather than working knowledge.
  • Specific creature Lore (e.g. Lupine Lore): A Kindred with three levels knows roughly what Kindred society as a whole has pieced together over centuries of contact — and about half of that received wisdom may be exaggerated or simply wrong.
  • Insider Lore (e.g. Garou Lore, as opposed to the outsider's "Lupine Lore"): Represents the "right stuff" — accurate names of tribes, the real story behind a weakness like silver, and a working knowledge of concepts like the Wyrm and spirits. This tier of knowledge is never free: a character with it should have visible scars, a story she isn't eager to tell about how she got it, and likely an active complication (an Ahroun hunting her, a blackmailer holding the secret over her head).

As a Storyteller, treat these tiers as a dial for pacing revelation in a crossover chronicle: award or gate Lore levels deliberately rather than letting general Occult substitute for specialized insider knowledge, and remember that even accurate knowledge came at a price for whoever taught it to the character.

vtmlarp.source: Storytellers Guide, "Those Who Hunt the Night"
